project.name: South Bethlehem / Lehigh Parking Monitor
project.type: Hackathon project (24 hours, software only, team of 3)
project.one_liner: A web app that shows where, when, and for how long parking spots are available around South Bethlehem and Lehigh University, using payment-session data (pay-by-hour sessions with per-zone time limits) as the occupancy signal.

current_state.repo: Scaffold is in place and tested: Supabase migration + seed (supabase/), FastAPI with stub and live modes (api/), simulator (simulator/), Next.js app with live map, plan, insights and demo pages (web/), Kiro steering (.kiro/steering/), CI and deploy workflows (.github/workflows/). Table names in the database are snake_case; the session table is named parking_session. Canonical static data is fixtures/zones.json. See README.md for cloud setup steps.

requirements.coverage: All parking types: Lehigh lots/garages, City of Bethlehem street meters, public/private garages.
requirements.detection: No hardware. Availability is estimated from pay-by-hour payment sessions. Each session has a zone, start time, and paid-until time; zones have time limits. Real session data is not publicly available, so the hackathon uses SYNTHETIC data calibrated to real rules (rates, limits, hours) and real demand patterns.

analytics.item: Occupancy heatmaps (by hour and day of week)
Availability prediction (chance of finding a spot at a given time and place)

domain_facts.fact: Two operators with different payment apps: Bethlehem Parking Authority (BPA) uses ParkMobile; Lehigh Parking Services uses Passport Parking (also Text2Park at Farrington Square after 4 PM and on weekends).

BPA runs a two-tier "ParkBethlehem" meter system on the South Side (2nd/3rd/4th St areas): time-limited premier spots, and "Park Once" spots at $1.50/hr with no time limit. Verify current premier rates on bethpark.org.
South Side BPA garages: Polk Street Garage (731 spaces, off E 3rd St, has real-time occupancy monitoring) and New Street Garage (324 S New St, about $1/hr, cashless).

Lehigh visitor parking: Zoellner garage Level 1 is pay-by-plate at about $1/hr, metered until 11 PM, 7 days a week; Levels 2-4 are permit-only unless event signage says otherwise. Alumni garage Level 1 is metered. Packer Ave has street meters.
Visitors of Lehigh students need the registered student to obtain a Daily Visitor Pass.
Lehigh runs event shuttles when an event exceeds about 1,050 expected attendees at Zoellner.
Calibration pattern from BPA: Main St and 3rd St (South Side) have chronic low turnover and shortage complaints; Morton Ave (South Side) consistently shows low occupancy.

Payment sessions are an imperfect proxy: coin/kiosk payers are invisible to app data, people leave early or overstay, and permit/placard parkers are not recorded. Use a per-zone correction factor and show confidence.

key_features.feature: Live map with zones colored by estimated occupancy.
"Opening soon": sessions expiring in the next 10-15 minutes in time-limited zones.
"Plan a visit": pick a destination (Zoellner, Goodman Stadium, Alumni Memorial, 3rd St shops) and an arrival time; get ranked parking options with price, walk time, and which app to pay with.
Insights page: heatmap by hour x day, dwell/turnover charts.
Demo control panel: buttons that spike simulated demand (game day, Family Weekend).
Privacy: no license plates stored; aggregates only.

tech_stack.frontend: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), shadcn/ui, Recharts, Leaflet loaded client-only. Deployed on Vercel.
tech_stack.backend: FastAPI (Python) deployed on Fly.io. Region ewr or iad. min_machines_running = 1 to avoid cold starts. Runs two processes: the API and the simulator worker.
tech_stack.database: Supabase (Postgres + PostGIS). Materialized views refreshed with pg_cron for analytics. Realtime enabled on Zone_Status. Row-level security on, public read-only; only FastAPI writes, using the service key kept in Fly secrets. Region us-east-1.
tech_stack.ai_tooling: Kiro (steering files, one spec per workstream, hooks, Supabase MCP server). This file is shared context for all AI tools.
tech_stack.principle: Let Postgres do the analytics, keep FastAPI thin, keep the frontend simple.
tech_stack.prediction_model: Start with average occupancy for each hour of the week multiplied by an event factor, computed in SQL. Add scikit-learn only if time remains after hour 16.

Schema + zones; API skeleton deployed to Fly; Next.js scaffold on Vercel with the map rendering zones.

team_plan.rules: No new features after hour 18. A working deploy at every milestone. Keep a recorded backup demo video. Sync every 4 hours (hours 6, 10, 14, 18).

repo_and_github.layout: .kiro/ (steering + specs, committed) .github/workflows/ api/ (Teammate A) web/ (Teammate B) supabase/migrations/ (Andrew; schema changes only here) simulator/ (Andrew) fixtures/ (shared contracts; announce any change) .env.example (variable names only)
repo_and_github.workflow: main is always deployable; no direct pushes. Short-lived branches named by lane (api/..., web/..., data/...). Open a PR every 1-3 hours. Squash merge. Pull main before opening a PR. CI must pass; reviews not required, but tag the team on any PR touching fixtures/ or supabase/migrations/.
repo_and_github.automation: GitHub Actions on PRs with path filters: web = tsc + ESLint; api = ruff + pytest. Vercel preview URL per PR. Fly deploy via flyctl on merge to main (FLY_API_TOKEN in repo secrets). Schema changes as SQL migrations applied with the Supabase CLI, never edited in the dashboard.
repo_and_github.tracking: Kiro tasks.md items become GitHub Issues labeled api/web/data; one GitHub Projects board; "Closes #N" in PRs.
repo_and_github.secrets: Real keys only in Vercel env, Fly secrets, and GitHub Actions secrets. .env* in .gitignore. Supabase anon key may reach the browser; the service key never leaves Fly.
repo_and_github.releases: Tag v0.1-mvp around hour 12 and v1.0-demo at feature freeze, for rollback.

kiro_setup.specs: data-model, analytics-api, map-ui, optional event-mode. Review data-model together first; the others depend on it.
kiro_setup.hooks: Schema SQL changes regenerate Supabase TS types and Pydantic models; FastAPI router changes regenerate the typed API client; run related tests or type checks on save.
kiro_setup.mcp: Supabase MCP server; a docs server (e.g. Context7) for current Next.js and Supabase docs.
kiro_setup.caution: Use spec mode only for the 3-4 big features; use chat for small tweaks.

1. LANDSCAPE City (BPA): runs meters + ParkMobile, permit programs, and garages. ParkBethlehem two-tier meters cover the South Side's 2nd/3rd/4th street areas: premier spots with time limits, and "Park Once" at $1.50/hr with no limit. Polk Street Garage (731 spaces, off E 3rd St, real-time occupancy monitoring); New Street Garage (324 S New St, $1/hr, cashless). BPA reports chronic shortage/low turnover on Main St and 3rd St (South Side), and low occupancy on Morton Ave.
Lehigh: uses PassportParking, a different app from the city's. Visitor options: pay-by-plate spaces, Zoellner garage L1 (kiosk or app, metered until 11 PM, 7 days; L2-4 permit-only), Text-to-Park at Farrington Square levels 1-2 after 4 PM and on weekends. Visitors of students need the student to obtain a Daily Visitor Pass. Event shuttles when Zoellner events exceed about 1,050 attendees.
2. CORE INSIGHT: payment sessions as a sensor Each session = zone + start + paid-until. Estimated occupancy = active sessions / capacity. Dwell = session length vs. limit. Turnover = new sessions per spot per hour. Key feature: "opening soon" = sessions expiring in the next 10-15 minutes. Gaps: coin payers, early departures, overstays, permit/placard parkers. Use a correction factor and confidence band. No public APIs exist; use synthetic data calibrated to real rules, and pitch a BPA/Lehigh partnership as the next step.
3. ANALYTICS MAPPING Heatmap (sessions/capacity per 15-min slot); prediction (average occupancy per hour of week x event factor); dwell & turnover; event/class-time impact using an event calendar.
